_meta.note: hits_to_kill uses the raw ROM 'health' byte and assumes no impervious flags and a single hitting weapon (slash/spin) at Fighter's Sword and Master Sword levels.

0x00.special_case_note: SpritePrep_Raven (usdasm/bank_06.asm:1930-1956, ROM $068963-$06896C) overrides the generic table at Prep time with a 2-entry [LightWorld, DarkWorld] table selected by $0FFF (world flag): damage byte $068963-4 (LW=$81 class1=half heart all mail, DW=$84 class4=1 heart all mail as PATCHED -- vanilla was $88 class8=up to 3 hearts on green mail), HP byte $068965-6 (LW=4, DW=8), prize byte $068967-8 (LW=pack6, DW=pack2 all-rupee). Oracle already patched the DW damage byte: Core/patches.asm:194-195 `org $068963 : db $81, $84` (comment 'Raven Damage (LW/DW)'), reducing DW damage class from 8 to 4. DW HP (8) is still double LW HP (4). Dive speed: Raven_Rise ($1DDDF6, usdasm/bank_1D.asm) and Raven_Attack ($1DDE21) both call Sprite_Apply/ProjectSpeedTowardsLink with a #$20 (32) speed constant, vs. Octorok's $06D367-D36B table (+-24) and Buzzblob's $06D8EE-D8F6 table (+-2/+-3) -- the Raven's dive is ~33% faster than an Octorok shot and ~10x the crawl speed of a Buzzblob. This is the 'fast bird'.

0x05.special_case_note: Sprites/Enemies/helmet_chuchu.asm declares !Health=$10(16) and !Damage=04(half heart) in its property block (lines 8-9), but Sprite_HelmetChuchu_Prep (lines 51-70) OVERRIDES HP at runtime from a sword-level-indexed table `.health: db $08,$0C,$0F,$10` (Fighter=8, Master=12, Tempered=15, Gold=16) -- HP scales up with the player's sword level, presumably to keep hits-to-kill roughly constant as sword damage increases. The generic table byte (16) is only what a level-4-sword-equipped Link would see; an Act I player with the Fighter's Sword actually faces 8 HP.

0x08.special_case_note: Sprites/Enemies/octorok.asm declares !Health=00 and !Damage=00 in its Set_Sprite_Properties block (lines 9-10) and its Sprite_Octorok_Prep does not set SprHealth/$0CD2 at runtime either -- so unlike vanilla (HP=2, usdasm/bank_0D.asm:6060) or Raven, THIS file's declared values (0/0) are what actually gets written to the ROM property tables at build time, if this is the copy of Sprite_Octorok_Prep/_Long registered by the last %Set_Sprite_Properties($08) call to assemble (registry.csv also lists no separate override -- check for a second octorok.asm-like file before relying on this). Read the ROM value below to confirm the built HP/damage for ID $08 rather than trusting source alone.
